tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA GeForce RTX sales Q2 fiscal 2027

events.content: NVIDIA GeForce RTX sales Q2 fiscal 2027

NVIDIA did **not separately disclose GeForce RTX sales** in Q2 fiscal 2027 (quarter ended July 26, 2026), because it replaced the standalone Gaming category with the broader **Edge Computing** platform. [[1]] 

The closest reported figure is **Edge Computing revenue of $7.2 billion**, up **13% sequentially** and **27% year over year**; this category includes GeForce/RTX-related business but is not a pure GeForce RTX sales measure. [[2]] 

For context, NVIDIA’s total Q2 FY2027 revenue was **$96.221 billion**, while Data Center revenue was **$89.0 billion**. [[3]] [[2]]

Related coverage:
NVIDIA no longer reports a standalone **GeForce/Gaming** revenue line beginning in FY2027; it has been incorporated into the broader **Edge Computing** category. [[1]] 

For the most recently reported quarter, **Q2 FY2027 ended July 26, 2026**, Edge Computing revenue was **$7.2 billion**, up **13% quarter over quarter** and **27% year over year**. [[2]]

tool_arguments.summary:
Research complete on NVIDIA's AI-related business performance per directive.

Key findings (Data Center segment only, most recent fiscal periods):
- Q2 FY2027 (ended July 26, 2026) Data Center revenue: **$89.0 billion**, up 18% quarter-over-quarter and 117% year-over-year. Source: S1.1.
- Growth drivers cited in the earnings release: sustained demand for AI infrastructure, large-scale cloud deployments, and growth in training/inference workloads across sectors.

Note on Gaming/GeForce: NVIDIA no longer reports a standalone GeForce/Gaming revenue line beginning FY2027; the category was replaced by the broader **Edge Computing** platform, which reported $7.2 billion in Q2 FY2027 (up 13% sequentially, 27% year-over-year). This edge figure includes GeForce/RTX-related business but is not a pure GeForce RTX sales metric. Sources: S3.1–S3.5.
